subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The chi-squared test is used in genetics to:
options: Calculate allele frequencies in a population
Measure the strength of a correlation
Determine whether observed phenotypic ratios differ significantly from expected ratios
questions.explain: Chi-squared compares observed and expected categorical data to test whether differences are due to chance.

questions.q: Continuous variation (e.g. human height) is typically caused by:
options: A single gene with two alleles
Many genes acting together (polygenic) plus environmental influence
questions.explain: Continuous variation is polygenic, with many genes and the environment producing a range of phenotypes.

questions.q: How does secondary succession differ from primary succession?
options: It begins on land that already has soil, e.g. after a fire
It never reaches a climax community
It involves no change in species over time
It begins on bare rock with no soil
questions.explain: Secondary succession starts where soil already exists, so it proceeds faster than primary succession.

questions.q: Natural selection leads to evolution because:
options: Individuals change their genes during their lifetime to suit the environment
Alleles that increase survival and reproduction become more frequent over generations
questions.explain: Differential survival and reproduction of advantageous alleles increases their frequency in the gene pool over time.

questions.q: Which sampling technique is most appropriate for estimating the population of a non-motile plant such as clover in a field?
questions.explain: Random quadrats are ideal for sessile organisms like plants, where individuals can be counted in a known area.

questions.q: Two genes are described as autosomally linked when they:
options: Are located on the X chromosome
Are located close together on the same autosome and tend to be inherited together
questions.explain: Linked genes lie on the same (non-sex) chromosome and tend to be inherited together rather than assorting independently.

questions.q: In the nitrogen cycle, which process converts atmospheric nitrogen gas into ammonia or ammonium ions?
questions.explain: Nitrogen fixation, carried out by bacteria such as Rhizobium and Azotobacter, converts N2 into ammonia.

questions.q: What is the correct sequence of conversions during nitrification?
options: Nitrogen gas then ammonia then nitrate
questions.explain: Nitrifying bacteria oxidise ammonia to nitrite (Nitrosomonas) and then nitrite to nitrate (Nitrobacter).

questions.q: In the mark-release-recapture method, the Lincoln index estimates population size N using which expression?
options: N = (first marked x second sample) / recaptured marked
N = recaptured marked / (first marked x second sample)
N = first marked + second sample - recaptured marked
questions.explain: Population = (number first marked x total in second sample) / number marked in the second sample.

questions.q: How is gross primary productivity (GPP) best defined?
options: The energy lost as heat by consumers
The total rate at which producers convert light energy into chemical energy
The biomass of all trophic levels combined
The energy remaining after respiratory losses
questions.explain: GPP is the total chemical energy fixed by producers before any is lost in respiration.

questions.q: Which genus of bacteria fixes nitrogen within the root nodules of leguminous plants?
questions.explain: Rhizobium lives mutualistically in legume root nodules and fixes atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia.

questions.q: The maximum population size an environment can support sustainably is known as the:
questions.explain: Carrying capacity is the maximum population an ecosystem's resources can support over a long period.
